items.stem: How did a book become a turning point in Richard Ebright’s life?
items.answer: The book “The Travels of Monarch X” opened the world of science for Richard. After reading it, he became interested in tracking the migration of butterflies. This interest led him to other projects and experiments. Finally, he became a great scientist.

items.stem: How did his mother help him?
items.answer: Richard’s mother proved to be a great help. She took him on trips and bought scientific equipments for him. She encouraged the scientific temperament in Richard. She spent all her time in setting out challenges for him. This helped him learn a lot. Read and Find Out - 2

items.stem: What lesson does Ebright learn when he does not win anything at a science fair?
items.answer: When Ebright does not win anything at a science fair, he learns that winner had tried to show real experiments.

items.stem: What experiments and projects does he then undertake ?
items.answer: He decided to do a real experiment. He tried to find the cause of a viral disease that kills nearly all monarch caterpillars every few years. Then he began his research into discovery of an unknown insect monarch.

items.stem: What are the qualities that go into making of a scientist ?
items.answer: There are many qualities (ingredients) that go into making of a scientist. Richard Ebright became a scientist since he was competitive and put in that extra effort. He had a first-rate mind with curiosity and mix in the will to win for the right reasons. Think About It

items.stem: How can one become a scientist, an economist, a historian Does it simply involve reading many books on the subject? Does it involve observing; thinking and doing experiments?
items.answer: One can perform a job to the best of his capabilities if one is really interested in it. Once we choose a goal or an aim, we should strive hard to achieve it. I think reading books is just one aspect of learning. This is an exercise in information gathering. It is how your brain processes the information that affects the degree of learning. The first and the foremost criterion to become a genius in one’s chosen field is to have great curiosity and unending hunger to discover more. Next criterion is a good sense of observation which helps you correlate your findings with what you see or experience in the real world. Experiments are must to test your findings against possible variables and in real life situations. And last, but not the least criterion is an urge to work really hard on your area of interest. Hard work is actually the key to success. One should have perseverance and strong will- power to achieve what one aspires to.

items.stem: You must have read about cells and DNA in your science books. Discuss Richard Ebright’s work in the light of what you have studied. If you get an opportunity to work like Richard Ebright on projects and experiments, which field would you like to work on and why?
items.answer: It is known that origin of life on earth is an established fact. By the process of gradual and continuous change, living organisms have evolved. After many number of experiments, scientists have established that gene is a segment of a large molecule called DNA. DNA carries genetic information from generation to generation. Richard Ebright worked on his basis. He raised flock of butterflies and raised the eggs of female Monarch. He studied the various stages of female Monarch. He further studied the cause of a viral disease that killed all Monarch caterpillars. Next he tried to find similarities between viceroy butterflies and monarchs. Study of insects’ hormone further give a new theory on the life of cells. Then he found the hormone behind butterfly’s full development. Thus, all these experiments led him to form a theory that cells grew from a monarch’s wings. The cell would divide and grow in a normal butterfly. If they were fed into a hormone from the gold spots. Thus, he proved a new cell theory which formed the blue print of DNA. If I am given a chance I would like to work in the sphere of stem cells which has a very wide range and would be a great keep for future. Talk About It

items.stem: Children everywhere wonder about the world around them. The questions they ask are the beginning of scientific inquiry. Given below are some questions that children in India have asked Professor Yash pal and Dr. Rahul Pal as reported in their book, ‘Discovered Questions’ (NCERT 2006) (i) What is DNA fingerprinting? What are its uses? (ii) How do honeybees identify their own honeycombs? (iii) Why does rain fall in drops? Can you answer these questions? You will find Professor Yash Pal’s and Dr Rahul Pal’s answers (as given in ‘Discovered Questions’) on page 75.
items.answer: Yes, we can answer these questions. The answers given by Dr. Yash Pal and Dr. Rahul Pal are very helpful. These answers have helped us from a great opinion and get deep into the concepts involved. (i) DNA carries genetic information to each living thing. DNA is inherited from our parents. DNA fingerprinting is important in Forensic Department. Even from a single hair or a drop of blood DNA can help us to find out the true culprit. (ii) Honeybees use such as a guide. They also appear to have a good memory. They try to find through a clever dance language. The dance indicates the direction and distance of the food source. Thus they have a well developed direction finding mechanism and a way of reckoning distance. (iii) Rain is formed as a result of condensation of vapour when air is cooled below the dew point. The raindrops start out as tiny ice crystals and on the way they collect moisture. The crystals change into water droplets and fall on the ground as drops.

items.stem: You also must have wondered about certain things around you. Share these questions with your class and try and answer them.
items.answer: There are many questions which are a question of worry for me: (i) Is there any material which does not burn in fire? (ii) Why do rain bearing clouds appear black? (iii) Why do some people snort during sleep?

items.stem: How can one say that Ebright’s curiosity/ inquisitiveness drove him to become a scientist ?
items.answer: In “The Making of a Scientist,” Ebright’s curiosity played a key role in shaping his scientific career. He constantly asked questions, searched for answers, and explored new ideas. His strong desire to understand the world encouraged him to conduct experiments and learn more, which eventually led him to become a scientist.

items.stem: Justify how Ebright’s mother played an important part in his becoming a scientist. Or How did Ebright’s mother encourage his interest in learning ? Or How did Ebright’s mother help him in becoming a scientist? Or How did Richard Ebright’s mother help him? Or Describe the role of Ebright’s mother in making him a scientist
items.answer: Ebright’s mother played a crucial role in his scientific journey by nurturing his curiosity and providing him with books and resources to explore his interests. She encouraged his inquisitive nature and instilled in him a love for learning, laying the foundation for his future success as a scientist.

items.stem: How important is curiosity to scientific exploration and discovery? Justify your answer with examples from the story ‘The Making of a Scientist’.
items.answer: Curiosity is extremely important to scientific exploration and discovery. It was Ebright’s curiosity that led him to collect items such as butterflies, fossils and coins. His desire to explore and constantly learn served as the foundation for his future scientific pursuits.

items.stem: What opinion did Mr. Weiherer, Ebright’s Social Science teacher have about him?
items.answer: Mr. Weiherer was of a great opinion about Ebright. According to him, Ebritht was competitive in a true sense as he didn’t want to just win the competition for the sake of winning it but he wanted to prove his experiments truly and contribute to the field of science.

items.stem: Richard’s mother was his companion and spent a lot of time with him. A parent should try to be a companion to a child. Justify.
items.answer: A parent can best judge a child’s needs and psychology. If a parent spends time with his child, like a friend, the child can feel confident, safe and motivated. Richard’s mother supported him by recognising his inclination towards butterflies that helped him in becoming a great scientist.

items.stem: Why do you think Mr. Weiherer was pleased that Richard Ebright not only put in the nightly research hours towards butterflies, but also his other interests?
items.answer: Mr. Weiherer was pleased that Ebright balanced academics as well as recreational pursuits, his hobbies etc. He was impressed by richard’s commitment towards his work. As a teacher, he wanted Ebright’s growth as a well-rounded personality.

items.stem: What lesson did Ebright learn when in the seventh grade he entered a country science fair? Or What lesson did Ebright learn when he could not win a prize at the science fair?
items.answer: Ebright exhibited slides of frog tissues at a country science fair. He did not get any prize. He learnt an important lesson that science is not just about display. It is about projects and real experiments. He began conducting experiments from that day onwards.

items.stem: Which book did Ebright’s mother get for him? How did it change his life?
items.answer: Ebright’s mother got him a children’s book called ‘The Travels of Monarch X.’

items.stem: What, according to Mr. Weiherer, makes Richard Ebright a winner ? Or According to Mr. Weiherer, what makes Richard Ebright a winner?
items.answer: According to Mr. Weiherer, Richard Ebright was not interested in winning for winnings sake or winning to get a prize. Rather, he was a winner because he wanted to do the best job he could.

items.stem: What were the factors which contributed to making Ebright a scientist?
items.answer: There are some genuine factors that contribute to making Ebright a scientist. First, he had a ‘driving curiosity along with a bright mind’ and zeal to do new ideas. Secondly, his mother’s encouragement and inspiration stood him in good stead to create interest in science. Finally, ‘The Travels of Monarch X’ opened the world of science to Ebright.

items.stem: Mention any two of Ebright’s contributions to the world of science.
items.answer: In his senior year in the high school, Ebright began to search an unkown hormone in the gold sports of the butterflies. He proved that the cells of a monard would develop into a normal butterfly wing only if they were fed the hormone from the gold spots. Another contribution of Ebright in the world of science is that he discovered how the cell could read the blue print of its DNA.

items.stem: Why did Richard Ebright give up tagging butterflies?
items.answer: Richard Ebright gave up tagging butterflies because he gradually lost interest in it. He found it absolutely a tedious work. Moreover, there was not much feedback. He tagged many butterflies but only two of them were captured. In fact, in the book, “The Travels of Monarch”, readers were asked by Dr. Frederick to tag butterflies for research.

items.stem: What other interests besides science did Richard Ebright pursue?
items.answer: Richard Bright had other interests besides science. To his credit, he became a champion debater and public speaker. He was also a good canoeist and an all-around outdoor person. He was also an expert photographer, particularly of nature and scientific exhibits.

items.stem: Which children’s book opened the world of science to the young Ebright?
items.answer: Ebright’s mother got him a children’s book called ‘The Travels of Monarch X’. That book, which told how monarch butterflies migrate to Central America, opened the world of science for the young Richard Ebright.

items.stem: From where had Richard Ebright graduated? What did he do immediately after graduation?
items.answer: Richard Ebright had graduated from Harvard with highest honours, being second in his class of 1,510. After graduation, he went on to become a graduate student researcher at Harvard Medical School.

items.stem: What can Ebright’s theory of cell life lead to if it is proved correct ?
items.answer: If Ebright’s theory of cell life is proved correct, it will be a big step towards understanding the process of life. It might also lead to new ideas for preventing some types of cancer and other diseases.

items.stem: Identify four values which Richard Ebright projected as a man of substance.
items.answer: Ebright was not only a good scientist but also a keen observer. He was good as a champion debater and a public speaker. He was an expert photographer particularly of nature and scientific exhibits.

items.stem: Why do viceroy butterflies copy monarchs ?
items.answer: Elbright’s theory proved that viceroys look like monarchs because monarchs don’t taste good to birds. But viceroys taste good to birds. Therefore, butterflies try to look like (copy) monarchs so that they can be saved.

items.stem: “When he saw those photos.” Which photos did he see and what discovery did this lead to ?
items.answer: He saw photos of the chemical structure of a hormone in the X-ray. This photo enabled him to answer one of the biology puzzles. His doubt on DNA was solved. He determined that DNA is the substance in the nucleus that controls heredity. So DNA was established to be the blueprint for life.

items.answer: Scienceforkidsblogger.com Monday, October 19, 2021 Science Is Real Science is present in every aspect of our life. science is not just a theory to learn from books. It has to be observed minutely because science is real. If you want to understand science in an easy and practical way, you should visit the kitchen or the garden in your house. Try to understand the science working behind the small objects present in our kitchens – lemon squeezer, garlic presser, grater etc. Have you ever asked your mother why the ginger turns to pink colour when lemon juice was poured on it? One can understand the concept of condensation by taking up the lid from a cooking utensil. If you have a scientific temperament you can experience that science is real and it pervades every field of our life.

items.stem: Richard’s mother had been invited to a talk show after Richard’s graduation from Harvard with the highest honours. You attended that talk show. Write the most memorable thing she spoke about and what you think it reveals about her.
items.answer: The Talk Show With Richard’s Mother Host : Well, Ms Ebright, how do you feel about Richard’s homecoming with the greatest Honours from Harvard. Mother : It feels really great! My son has brought honours to me and our country. Host : Was he a special child or an average child? Mother : He was absolutely an average child in his school. He used to observe things happening in nature very keenly and It helped him a lot. He kept himself busy researching whatever fascinated him. Host : Do you want to give any parenting tips? Mother : Keep your kids busy with constructive ideas and try to understand their talent at the initial stage itself. Host : Do you see any change in Richard’s attitude now? Mother : Oh yes, he is more sincere, more determined and more dedicated now.

items.answer: Letter of gratitude as Richard Harvard University Cambridge Massachusetts 20 September 1981 Mrs Ebright Reading Pennsylvania Dear Mom, It has been long since I have written to you. You will be glad to know that all the teachers here praise me for my real knowledge of Science. You know, all the credit goes to you. I can never forget your friendly and fun-filled ways to enable me to learn new things. The evenings we spent together at the dining table were proved to be most helpful. I don’t know how you managed to buy those toys and materials after my father’s death. Your foresightedness in buying the ‘The Migration of Monarch’ changed my life all the way for good. Mumma, I am blessed to have a mother like you. I wish you to be my mother in every birth. Take care Goodbye Your loving son Richie

items.stem: Albert Einstein said, ‘The important thing is to never stop questioning.’ Richard was a genius who proved this quote true. Justify.
items.answer: Surely, this statement is true in the case of Richard Ebright because he always kept himself busy in constructive experiments since his early childhood. Richard had a habit of asking questions about new things and his mother answered all his questions in the most satisfying manner. This question and answer round turned into a habit in Richard and he kept on probing things. His scientific bent of mind led him to carry on experiments after experiment and reach a purposeful conclusion. Although to reach his goal he was helped by many people in his journey, especially his mother whose contribution is commendable. He had patiently waited for almost a year to study butterflies’ migration. This shows that he never stopped midway and finally became a great scientist.

items.stem: Imagine you are Richard. You have been invited by Mr Weiherer to deliver a short address to the students at your erstwhile school. You have been asked to encourage them to take an interest in the study of Science and how research in Science can help the world. Write that short speech.
items.answer: Hello, my dear young friends It is an honour to stand amongst you and say a few words on how the study of science changed my life. I think curiosity is the key to invention. You know, as a child, I was always curious to know why things happened in a particular way. Curiosity led me to experiment and experiments led me to conclusions and eventually inventions. You must be knowing that all the inventions are backed by a series of research by great scientists. Scientific developments have created all the facilities we enjoy in our lives today. From a small needle to a big aeroplane everything is the product of scientists’ hard work and patience. I feel that every child should take up the study of science in school to grow with confidence in life. Stop cramming and start experimenting.

items.stem: Richard Ebright displayed a well-rounded personality. Do you agree ? Elucidate in the context of the given text.
items.answer: Richard’s genius was obvious by the time he was in his second grade. He managed to collect all twenty-five species of butterflies around his hometown and classify them. He also loved to collect coins, fossils and rocks. Science was not his only passion. He was an active member of his school’s oratory club and model United Nations club and was an effective debater and a public speaker. He loved photography as well. He was an enthusiastic canoeist and an all- around outdoors person. Learning was easy for him. So he found it simple to devote time and energy to many other interests. He became a champion in whatever he did. He believed in the spirit of competition to win. But, he did not wish to defeat others just to win. He wanted to win to do his best. Thus, he displayed a well-rounded personality.

items.stem: What other interests besides science did Richad Ebright pursue? What opinion did Mr. Weiherer, his social studies teacher, have about Ebright? Or What opinion did Mr Weiherer, his social studies teacher, have about Ebright?
items.answer: Besides science, Richard Ebright had also interest in other fields. He also became a champion debater and public speaker. He was a good canoeist and an all-round outdoors-person. He was an expert photographer, particularly of nature and scientific exhibits. In high school, Richard Ebright was a straight-A student. He rendered a lot of energy towards the Debating and Model United Nations Club. Mr Weiherer, his social studies teacher, cherished a high opinion about Richard Ebright. He admired for the extra efforts that Richard gave for doing debate research besides his research with butterflies and other interests. Mr Weiherer emphasized that Richard was winning because he wanted to do the best job he could do. For the right reasons, he wanted to be the best of the best.

items.stem: What was the impact of the book ‘The Travels of Monarch X’ on Richard Ebright ?
items.answer: Richard Ebright had started collecting butterflies when he was in kindergarten. So, to maintain his interest in this field in his later years, his mother had got him a children’s book called ‘The Travels of Monarch X.’ This book had told how monarch butterflies migrate to Central America. The impact of this book was so strong on Ebright’s mind that it opened the world of science for him. At the end of this book, readers had been invited to help study butterfly migrations. They had been asked to tag butterflies for research by Dr. Frederick A. Urquhart of the university of Toronto, Canada. Ebright’s mother wrote to Dr. Urquhart, and soon Ebright was also taking part in the study by attaching light adhesive tags to the wings of the monarchs. According to the research, anyone who found a tagged butterfly was asked to send the tag to Dr. Urquhart. Ultimately, it was Richard’s fascination for butterflies that opened the world of science to him. It also indirectly led to his theory on how cells work.

items.stem: Dr Urquhart contributed significantly to Ebright’s growth as a scientist. Explain.
items.answer: Richard had become bored with collecting butterflies. His mother got him a book on the migration of butterflies. Richard came in contact with Dr. Urquhart through the book. Dr. Urquhart directed him to study the migration pattern of butterflies. When he did not win any prize in the science fair in seventh grade, he again wrote to Dr Urquhart to guide him. The scientist gave him many suggestions for new experiments. Richard performed these experiments throughout his high school and won many prizes. Later, he worked on why bright spots are found on a monarch pupa, motivated by Dr. Urquhart. It led to the discovery of a new hormone. The discovery of this new hormone further led to an important theory. The theory was about how cells read their DNA. In this way Dr. Urquhart proved to be his true mentor.
